10939-after-waterloo-reminiscences-of-eu.creator: Major W.E. Frye
10939-after-waterloo-reminiscences-of-eu.description: A book by Major W.E. Frye. From Bruxelles to Paris--Restoration of Louis XVIII--The officers of the allied armies--The Palais Royal--The Louvre--Protest of the author against the proposed despoiling of the French Museums--Unjust strictures against Napoleon's military policy--The _cant_ about revolutionary robberies--The Grand Opera--Monuments in Paris--The Champs Elysées--Saint-Cloud--The Hôtel des Invalides--The Luxembourg--General Labédoyère--Priests and emigrants--Prussian Plunder--Handsome behaviour of the English officers--Reminiscences of Eton--Versailles.

arxiv-2001-11424.title: On the stress overshoot in cluster crystals under shear
arxiv-2001-11424.creator: G.P. Shrivastav, G. Kahl
arxiv-2001-11424.description: Abstract Using non-equilibrium molecular dynamics simulations we study the yielding behaviour of a model cluster crystal formed by ultrasoft particles under shear. We investigate the evolution of stress as a function of strain for different shear rates, γ ˙ \dot{\gamma} , and temperatures.

arxiv-2205-08972.title: The Structure of Configurations in One-Dimensional Majority Cellular Automata: From Cell Stability to Configuration Periodicity
arxiv-2205-08972.creator: Yonatan Nakar, Dana Ron
arxiv-2205-08972.description: Abstract We study the dynamics of (synchronous) one-dimensional cellular automata with cyclical boundary conditions that evolve according to the majority rule with radius r r . We introduce a notion that we term cell stability with which we express the structure of the possible configurations that could emerge in this setting.

arxiv-2212-07379.title: The finite sample performance of instrumental variable-based estimators of the Local Average Treatment Effect when controlling for covariates
arxiv-2212-07379.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by . This paper investigates the finite sample performance of a range of parametric, semi-parametric, and non-parametric instrumental variable estimators when controlling for a fixed set of covariates to evaluate the local average treatment effect. Our simulation designs are based on empirical labor market data from the US and vary in several dimensions, including effect heterogeneity, instrument selectivity, instrument strength, outcome distribution, and sample size.

arxiv-2401-14845.title: Adaptive Point Transformer Journal: Neural Networks
arxiv-2401-14845.creator: Alessandro Baiocchi, Indro Spinelli, Alessandro Nicolosi, Simone Scardapane
arxiv-2401-14845.description: Abstract The recent surge in 3D data acquisition has spurred the development of geometric deep learning models for point cloud processing, boosted by the remarkable success of transformers in natural language processing. While point cloud transformers (PTs) have achieved impressive results recently, their quadratic scaling with respect to the point cloud size poses a significant scalability challenge for real-world applications.

arxiv-2411-03811.title: The natural stability of autonomous morphology: How an attraction–repulsion dynamic emerges from paradigm cell filling
arxiv-2411-03811.creator: Erich Round, Louise Esher, Sacha Beniamine
arxiv-2411-03811.description: Abstract Autonomous morphology, such as inflection class systems and paradigmatic distribution patterns, is widespread and diachronically resilient in natural language. Why this should be so has remained unclear given that autonomous morphology imposes learning costs, offers no clear benefit relative to its absence and could easily be removed by the analogical forces which are constantly reshaping it.

arxiv-2411-13652.title: Soft limits of gluon amplitudes in holography and cosmology
arxiv-2411-13652.creator: Soner Albayrak , , {}^{\text{\faIconFromMacro{faPencil}}\,,\,\text{\faIconFromMacro{faPencilSquare}}\,,\,\text{\faIconFromMacro{faPencilSquareO}}}, Savan Kharel
arxiv-2411-13652.description: Abstract In this work, we extend the study of soft limits to (Anti) de Sitter spaces, investigating the analytic structure of holographic gluon correlators as part of a broader effort to reveal new symmetries and fundamental structures in gauge theories.

arxiv-2501-05316.title: The CO-Fuelled Time Machine: Tracing Birth Conditions and Terrestrial Planet Formation Outcomes in HD 163296 through Pebble Drift-induced CO Enhancements 2025 The CO-Fuelled Time Machine: Tracing Birth Conditions and Terrestrial Planet Formation Outcomes in HD 163296 through Pebble Drift-induced CO
arxiv-2501-05316.creator: Joe Williams, Sebastiaan Krijt
arxiv-2501-05316.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Joe Williams, Sebastiaan Krijt. The architecture and composition of planetary systems are thought to be strongly influenced by the transport and delivery of dust and volatiles via ices on pebbles during the planet formation phase in protoplanetary discs. Understanding these transport mechanisms is crucial in building a comprehensive picture of planet formation, including material and chemical budget; constraining the birth properties of these discs is a key step in this process.

arxiv-2501-17041.title: Benchmarking Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks for Signal Classification in Simulated Gamma-Ray Burst Detection
arxiv-2501-17041.creator: Farida Farsian, Nicoló Parmiggiani, Alessandro Rizzo, Gabriele Panebianco, Andrea Bulgarelli, Francesco Schilliró, Carlo Burigana, Vincenzo Cardone, Luca Cappelli, Massimo Meneghetti, Giuseppe Murante, Giuseppe Sarracino, Roberto Scaramella, Vincenzo Testa, Tiziana Trombetti
arxiv-2501-17041.description: Abstract This study evaluates the use of Quantum Convolutional Neural Networks (QCNNs) for identifying signals resembling Gamma-Ray Bursts (GRBs) within simulated astrophysical datasets in the form of light curves. The task addressed here focuses on distinguishing GRB-like signals from background noise in simulated Cherenkov Telescope Array Observatory (CTAO) data, the next-generation astrophysical observatory for very high-energy gamma-ray science.

arxiv-2503-09848.title: A second-order numerical scheme for optimal control of non-linear Fokker–Planck equations and applications in social dynamics
arxiv-2503-09848.creator: G. Albi, E. Calzola
arxiv-2503-09848.description: Abstract In this work, we present a second-order numerical scheme to address the solution of optimal control problems constrained by the evolution of nonlinear Fokker–Planck equations arising from socio–economic dynamics. In order to design an appropriate numerical scheme for control realization, a coupled forward-backward system is derived based on the associated optimality conditions.

arxiv-2508-03377.title: The Subgraphs of Order Six of the Family of Strongly Regular Graphs with Parameters λ = 1 \lambda=1 and μ = 2 \mu=2
arxiv-2508-03377.creator: Reimbay Reimbayev
arxiv-2508-03377.description: Abstract Strongly regular graphs are highly symmetrical and can be described fully with just a few parameters yet the existence of many of them is still under the question. Due to this uncertainty, it is of immense interest to study their structure, in particular to obtain all the possible subgraphs of lower order.

pmc-11510662.title: Prescribing Pattern and Safety Profile of Biological Agents for Psoriasis in Real-World Practice: A Four-Year Calabrian Pharmacovigilance Analysis
pmc-11510662.creator: Caterina De Sarro, Francesca Bosco, Agnese Gagliardi, Lorenza Guarnieri, Stefano Ruga, Antonio Fabiano, Laura Costantino, Antonio Leo, Caterina Palleria, Chiara Verduci, Vincenzo Rania, Michael Ashour, Luca Gallelli, Rita Citraro, Giovambattista De Sarro
pmc-11510662.description: Background: The treatment of psoriasis has made considerable progress with biologicals, including tumor necrosis factor inhibitors, and recently, monoclonal antibodies inhibiting directly interleukin (IL) 17, IL-23, or both IL-12/23. Newer biologicals are directed to the interleukin pathway and appear to improve complete or near-complete clearance. The newer biologicals have also been shown to have an excellent safety profile.

pmc-11526722.title: Prevalence of non-smoking chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and its risk factors in China: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-11526722.creator: Yue Zhang, Xiaoyan Gai, Hongling Chu, Jingge Qu, Liang Li, Yongchang Sun
pmc-11526722.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundChronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) is a prevalent chronic disorder in China, impacting a significant proportion of individuals aged > 40 years. In China, the prevalence of and risk factors for COPD among non-smokers remain largely unexplored.

pmc-11626622.title: Control of hypercapnia and mortality in home mechanical ventilation: the population-based DISCOVERY study
pmc-11626622.creator: Andreas Palm, Magnus Ekström, Össur Emilsson, Karin Ersson, Mirjam Ljunggren, Josefin Sundh, Ludger Grote
pmc-11626622.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundStudies on the survival of patients with home mechanical ventilation (HMV) are sparse. We aimed to analyse the impact of controlled hypercapnia on survival over 27 years among patients with HMV in Sweden.Study design and methodsPopulation-based cohort study of adult patients starting HMV in the Swedish Registry for Respiratory Failure (Swedevox) during 1996–2022 cross-linked with the National Cause of Death registry.

Twitter Avatar which is the profile image of the user, is initially uploaded when the user takes his account and never changes as long as the user changes it.

pmc-12606678.title: Platelet Count of Zero: A Case of Vancomycin-Induced Immune Thrombocytopenia
pmc-12606678.creator: Shiv B Gakhar, Adam Hurwitz, Colton Sellars, Andrew Willinger, Melanie Cheing
pmc-12606678.description: Immune thrombocytopenia (ITP) is an acquired hematologic disorder marked by immune-mediated destruction of platelets, leading to profound thrombocytopenia and increased bleeding risk. Drug-induced immune thrombocytopenia (DITP), specifically vancomycin-induced immune thrombocytopenia (VIIT), is a rare but serious adverse drug reaction, caused by drug-dependent antibodies that accelerate platelet clearance.

pmc-13156594.title: Atypical presentation of intraosseous plasmacytoma in a patient with POEMS syndrome
pmc-13156594.creator: Jude Kolodisner, Matthew Scarsbrook, Gabriella Mamo, Tyson Chadaz
pmc-13156594.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). POEMS syndrome is an uncommon paraneoplastic syndrome featuring polyneuropathy, organomegaly, endocrinopathy, monoclonal gammopathy, and skin changes. POEMS syndrome in conjunction with plasmacytoma is a particularly rare finding, mostly featured only in case reports and small case series. We present a case of a 52-year-old female with POEMS syndrome with a biopsy-proven solitary bone plasmacytoma of the scapula demonstrating atypical imaging features.

pmc-13203005.title: Comparative performance of risk prediction models for kidney disease: an external validation using 0.5 million UK Biobank participants
pmc-13203005.creator: Yikun Zhang, Chun Hin Chan, Hin Lai Ivan Lam, David Bishai, Philip Clarke, Sydney C.W. Tang, Jianchao Quan
pmc-13203005.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ObjectiveTo compare the external validation performance of existing kidney disease risk prediction models for the general population, individuals with type 2 diabetes, and across various subgroups.Materials and methodsWe identified and compared 16 risk prediction models for chronic kidney disease (CKD) or kidney failure from 3 recent systematic reviews (7 models for the whole population, 9 models specific for type 2 diabetes). We analysed 497,896 adults (age 38–73) in the UK Biobank data; of which 4·7% (n = 23,298) had type 2 diabetes.

pmc-13629140.title: Curcumin-rich plant material production through a robust and reproducible micropropagation protocol
pmc-13629140.creator: Gilles Habib Todjro Cacaï, Serge Sètondji Houedjissin, Jérôme Anani Houngue, Bamidélé Viviane Alakè Ogounchi, Jaurès Riwan Uriel Kouke, Corneille Ahanhanzo
pmc-13629140.description: Curcuma longa Linné is a widely valued spice due to its nutritional and therapeutic properties. Its production methods, vulnerability to diseases, and increasing anthropogenic pressure contribute to the limited availability of planting materials. This study aims to develop a micropropagation protocol that ensures the production of curcumin-rich planting stocks.
